title: Similes of Nostalgia, Loss, and Illusion with mintha

sections.title: Expressing Cultural and Sensory Distance
sections.content: When discussing historical degradation, standardization, or aesthetic loss, the comparative conjunction 'mintha' introduces hypothetical clauses contrasting appearances with reality. The structure 'úgy viselkedtek / úgy tűnt, mintha...' paired with past conditional forms (ige + volna) expresses counterfactual nostalgia or an illusion that masked a deeper absence.

sections.title: Past Counterfactual Subordination with mintha + volna
sections.content: To express past hypothetical situations, Hungarian uses the past conditional: 'mintha elfelejtették volna' (as if they had forgotten), 'mintha megszűnt volna' (as if it had ceased), 'mintha soha nem létezett volna' (as if it had never existed). In sensory critique, this conveys an impression of artificiality: 'olyan íze volt, mintha szintetikus aromákból keverték volna ki'.

sections.title: Counterfactual Similes of Nostalgia
rows: Úgy tűnt, mintha a hagyományok elvesztek volna.
It seemed as if traditions had been lost.
Olyan íze volt az ételnek, mintha menzán főzték volna.
The food tasted as if it had been cooked in a canteen.
Úgy tettek, mintha minden a legnagyobb rendben volna.
They acted as if everything were in the greatest order.

items.spanish: Az éttermek szabványosított ételei olyan egyhangúak voltak, mintha egyetlen receptkönyvből másolták volna az összes fogást.
items.english: The standardized dishes of the restaurants were so monotonous as if they had copied all dishes from a single recipe book.

items.spanish: A fogyasztók évtizedekig úgy ittak bort, mintha a hegyaljai terroir gazdagsága soha nem létezett volna.
items.english: For decades consumers drank wine as if the richness of Hegyalja terroir had never existed.

items.spanish: A brüsszeli magyar pavilonban a vendégek úgy érezték magukat, mintha megelevenedett volna a békebeli Budapest.
items.english: In the Hungarian pavilion in Brussels, guests felt as if peaceful prewar Budapest had come alive.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: In past-tense contexts, use the past conditional with 'volna': 'mintha elveszett volna' (as if it had been lost), rather than present conditional 'elveszne'.
